doc.title: Zutty Singleton and Marge Singleton Interview, 1969-02-08

chapter: Jelly Roll Morton in Chicago and early sightings
title: Visiting Louis and Lil's Chicago home with Jelly Roll Morton
summary: Zutty recalls meeting Jelly Roll Morton on South Parkway in Chicago and going to Louis and Lil's house, where Jelly played their new baby grand. Much of the block is garbled.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, one particular time I remember Jelly Man. Lou and I were playing with Carol Dickinson's band at the Savoy, you know, in Chicago. So we had rehearsal that day. So after rehearsal, we were walking down South Parkway and who we ran into but Jelly. Boy, the old Jelly was so sharp that they had on a pale pink silk shirt and a Panama hat looked like it cost about 25 hours in those days, you know. It was real good, you know. And I noticed that diamond in his tooth, you know. And Louis started talking and we jaw blocked quite a while. And Louis said, hey, Jelly, how about coming over to the house? I said, Lil got a brand new baby grand and I believe it was a Steinway, you know. So Jelly said, well, come on, let's go. And we went on over to Louis' house, you know. And he and Lil, they lived on 44th Street near South Parkway in Chicago. So boy, old Jelly got down to that piano. Oh, and he was crazy about it, you know. So he started playing and he'd switch around on the stool and tell us that I still have a few sweatiest little man from and I am a queen of the love and the love dear 27 and 28 between that time. Because we recorded, you know, he'd tell me if he wanted to make a trio record, but he was waiting for Duke Ellington. He wanted to be God. Bonnie be God, he and myself, you know. So, you know, sports, right? You know, we're the most serious sports, right? I didn't like this. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. You know where I met Jolly Steve Lewis? Give my shit out, old man.
